Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (625 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) bought no bitcoin last week and sold no stock to fund newly introduced purchases, leaving its holdings unchanged at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing.
  • The Dallas-based company reported that its bitcoin count was unchanged between Nov.
  • The pause follows a slowdown from the October sprint that built the stack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) bought no bitcoin last week and sold no stock to fund newly introduced purchases, leaving its holdings unchanged at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing.

The Dallas-based company reported that its bitcoin count was unchanged between Nov. 13 and Nov. 20. It sold no Class A common shares, no SATA preferred shares and no SATS preferred shares in its at-the-market programs from the Nov. 13 close through the Nov. 20 close.

The pause follows a slowdown from the October sprint that built the stack. Strive bought 251 bitcoin for $17.5 million the prior week at an average of $69,853 per coin, after adding just 29 coins the week before that.

Bitcoin traded near $61,000 on Coinbase on Monday afternoon. That is about 12.6% below the $69,853 average Strive paid for its most recent purchase. At that price, the 43,404-coin stack is worth roughly $2.65 billion.

Industry observers note that the filing gives no reason for the pause, and the company has not noted whether it plans to resume weekly buying. Strive has typically disclosed its holdings on Mondays, so next week’s update will show whether the stack grows again.

Most of the stack was built promptly. Strive held 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and acquired 15,124 more between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, including a single 6,182-coin purchase. The firm closed a registered offering of 7 million SATS shares on Oct. 20 for about $609 million in net proceeds, which funded much of that run.

Sources indicate that strive’s cash and cash equivalents slipped to $462.4 million as of Nov. 20 from $465.3 million a week earlier, a decline of $2.9 million. The filing does not break out what drove the change.

Industry observers note that the company also still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred stock. The fair value of that position fell to $47.3 million from $50.5 million, a drop of about $3.2 million, with the share count unchanged.

In a recent development, share counts were also flat. Strive reported 118,133,002 Class A shares and 9,198,107 Class B shares, for 127,331,109 effective common shares. Outstanding preferred stood at 14,030,176 shares of SATA and 7,141,037 shares of SATS, the 15% perpetual preferred it has used to fund most of its purchases.

Strive’s holdings rose from 43,153 bitcoin on Nov. 6 to 43,404 on Nov. 13, and the filing demonstrates no change since. With no common or preferred stock sold, the tech giant raised no new capital through its offering programs last week, which left cash as its main resource for dividends and operations.

Recent findings suggest that strive shares were trading near $15.55 at 3:56 p.m. ET on Monday, up about 7.1% from Friday’s close of $14.51, according to Yahoo Finance. The stock opened near $17.64, a gain of more than 20%, and gave back much of it through the session.

In a recent development, the swing tracked bitcoin-linked stocks broadly after Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang and sent equities sharply higher, a move Bitcoin Magazine covered earlier Monday. Bitcoin spiked above $64,000 in the morning before sliding back toward $61,000 during U.S. trading hours.

The stock has lost much of its October run. ASST closed at $30.75 on Oct. 21, so Monday’s price is about 49% lower. It is still roughly 5% above its 2025 year-end close of $14.76.

Strive’s preferred stocks remain a central part of its model. On Nov. 12, the board raised the SATA dividend rate to 13.25% for periods beginning Dec. 1, while SATS continues to pay 15%. Both pay daily cash dividends, so the company’s cash balance funds a steady outflow even in weeks without purchases.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $61,000.

Industry News: Mauviel's Copper Cookware Is 25% Off For Black Friday

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (492 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are a few covetable luxury goods you’ll see pop up again and again in AD’s home tours: a Moccamaster coffee maker, a Nordic Knots rug, and Mauviel copper cookware, to name a few.
  • Industry observers note that I’m a recent convert; I bought my Mauviel frying pan mostly to elevate the aesthetic of my kitchen, with a suspicion that the tool would also function as a fantastic piece of cookware, particularly for my beloved morning ritual of frying up an egg for breakfast.
  • That excellent cooking capability is largely due to the construction and craftsmanship of the goods, which have a long history as a French culinary staple.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are a few covetable luxury goods you’ll see pop up again and again in AD’s home tours: a Moccamaster coffee maker, a Nordic Knots rug, and Mauviel copper cookware, to name a few. As seen in this Sag Harbor home, this Parisian pied-à-terre, this Westchester residence, and this Connecticut country retreat, Mauviel is something of a status symbol in kitchens. Much like a Le Creuset Dutch oven out on display, spying a few copper pans from the French brand hanging from a rail signals that “Great Taste Lives Here.” And this week marks a good opportunity to join the club, with Mauviel sets and individual pieces up to 30% off for Black Friday at Williams Sonoma and on Shop.

Industry observers note that I’m a recent convert; I bought my Mauviel frying pan mostly to elevate the aesthetic of my kitchen, with a suspicion that the tool would also function as a fantastic piece of cookware, particularly for my beloved morning ritual of frying up an egg for breakfast. Of course it does. Unlike some of my ceramic pans that catch and dry out an egg, the Mauviel has given me no trouble, delivering me the most perfect eggs to date I’ve ever cooked. Even against my stainless-steel pans (which I do love very much), these heat a bit more swiftly and evenly.

That excellent cooking capability is largely due to the construction and craftsmanship of the goods, which have a long history as a French culinary staple. Mauviel has made copper cookware since 1830 in Villedieu-les-Poêles, a town in Normandy with an enduring history of copper manufacturing; the pieces are still handcrafted there. As far as their makeup, the M’150 B pieces are, for example, 1.5 millimeters thick and constructed of a 90% polished copper exterior and a 10% stainless-steel interior. They heat evenly; are immediately responsive to heat adjustments; and work on gas, electric, and ceramic cooktops.

The pans partners with a copper kettle on the stove in this Portland manse by Jessica Helgerson.

It has been revealed that the copper treasures do, however, require care. They’re not nonstick pots and pans, so you need a little oil or butter to get any slip. They’re hand-wash only, and Mauviel advises against using them for long stretches on high heat or leaving them empty on a hot burner. I don’t polish mine, simply because I don’t own any copper polish. The wear demonstrates swiftly, and I like that, though if AD were shooting my house, maybe I’d like it less.

Sources indicate that the Black Friday markdowns run across the line: my copper fry pan is going for $280 in the 10-inch size (25% off), a 2.5-quart sauce pan is $450 (29% off), and a 15-piece cookware set is $3,000 (32% off). For anyone who cooks every day, it’s a hard gift to beat. I, for one, now can’t imagine frying my eggs any other way.

  • Recent findings suggest that morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner.
  • Industry observers note that nvidia closed Friday at $125.53, down 47.5% from its October high, which works out to roughly $2.7 trillion of market value gone in seven weeks.
  • Industry observers note that the Nasdaq dropped 10% on the week, its worst since 2020, erasing its entire 2026 gain and shedding about $8.7 trillion since October 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

Industry observers note that nvidia closed Friday at $125.53, down 47.5% from its October high, which works out to roughly $2.7 trillion of market value gone in seven weeks. The company beat earnings last week and guided revenue higher, and the stock still fell 23% across the five sessions.

Industry observers note that the Nasdaq dropped 10% on the week, its worst since 2020, erasing its entire 2026 gain and shedding about $8.7 trillion since October 6. The S&P and Dow both closed in correction, AMD lost 20.5%, and CoreWeave now trades below its IPO price. Bank of America’s fund manager survey demonstrated investors cutting tech exposure by the most since 2006, with 52% expecting at least one major hyperscaler to announce a capex cut inside six months.

Polymarket traders put 54% odds that the AI bubble will burst in 2026.

According to recent reports, crypto rode the same elevator down. Bitcoin hit roughly $55,100 Friday night, its lowest level since 2024 and marking a new cycle low, 56% off last October’s peak. Fear and Greed printed 9 and ETFs bled $1.79 billion on the week. It’s now tracking toward two consecutive down years, which has never happened before.

Then came the weekend bounce. Bitcoin reclaimed $60,000 and sits over $61,000 this morning; ETH is back above $1,710, and even Anthropic, down 9% Friday, quotes near $90 on Hyperliquid’s perp, still above its $83 offer.

Two explanations landed over the weekend.

Sources indicate that U.S. President Donald Trump posted Sunday that the market is down $6 trillion since the Democrats’ “rather strange” win on November 3, that the Nasdaq is down 20%, and that it’s “100% due to” Democratic policy. Looks like no Trump bailout is coming anytime soon.

Elon Musk’s version is more useful. He warned Saturday that the cash shortage next year is “going to be nuts,” because even a few months of lag between paying for compute and earning revenue off it means hundreds of billions in incremental working capital. Then the question: where will that come from?

It has been revealed that that’s a funding problem rather than a valuation one, and it lands harder coming from him. SpaceX reportedly sold $32 billion of bonds last week to buy Nvidia chips, so he’s describing a squeeze he’s already borrowing into.

So where does this leave us? The Fed meets December 8th and 9th with the market pricing a hike into all of this. Gas prices just hit an eight-month low ahead of Thanksgiving, down about 15% in a month, which should take some pressure off the headline print. The catch is that pump prices are still running 18% above last year, and core CPI, the number Waller actually cited when he floated fifty basis points, strips energy out entirely. Any relief has to come from shelter and services cooling instead.

Sources indicate that perhaps the Fed provides some. Whether it’s enough to stop the bleeding, only time will tell.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Recent findings suggest that THE BEST GIFTS for outdoorsmen aren’t typically the shiniest or the fanciest gadgets, but rather rugged and functional. What's great about the world we live in now is you don't have to be a certified outdoorsman to receive outdoor gifts. Any guy who's spending time outside will enjoy the latest and greatest outdoor gear.

According to recent reports, the best outdoor gifts also function as great gifts for dads, smart gifts for men, and (of course) perfect gifts for camping. Whether he’s a nature novice or a seasoned mountain man chopping his own wood, we've collected all our field notes from rigorous testing in the past year to assemble the best gifts for outdoorsmen at every level and price point. Keep scrolling to get to the good stuff and don't put it off, as we're getting down to the wire for holiday gifting.

It has been revealed that these electric hand warmers hold about 16 hours of steady warmth. What's cool is they stick together via a magnet for easy storage so you'll never lose one and be without it.

Read More: My Favorite Pieces of Hiking Gear.

The Lifestraw Peak Series will eliminate approximately 99.999 percent of bacteria, parasites, microplastics, sand, and dirt. Gift this personal water filter as a stocking stuffer, or buy multiple and pass them out to all of the outdoorsmen in your life.

Sources indicate that nike blew us away with the release of this trail running shoe. Don’t be fooled by the low profile, because while sleek, this shoe is grippy, grounded, and up for just about any terrain you throw at it. We liked the extra toe room as well as how the sole functions more like shock absorbers than the base of a shoe, taking bump after bump while keeping your feet plenty comfortable. Whether you’re barreling down a hill or zigzagging up a steep slope, these shoes will give you an added boost and keep you both cool and stable.

In a recent development, now, this is a cool adventure gift. The Nanopresso Portable Espresso Maker brings you top-quality coffee wherever you go. Just bring your favorite coffee grounds, add hot water, and this little machine does the rest. As you pump, the pressure is made, and thus, so is your drink. And at smaller than the size of a thermos, you can fit this just about anywhere.

Ah, the rancher jacket. It’s a double-sided gem, one that both looks the part but delivers even in the most rugged conditions. This fine option from Flint and Tinder is flannel-lined to fend off the chilly bite, as well as quilted and stuffed with insulation for good measure. That means even the nastiest of winds won’t bother him while he’s out chopping wood for the campfire. The roomy build means he can layer appropriately underneath and the fact that it reveals a little age with a nice patina over time is a massive plus. He’ll be way ready for winter with his jacket.

Take all the bear-, weather-, and bomb-proofness of Yeti’s Loadout GoBox (and coolers) and shrink it down to a 1-liter case that’s perfect for phones, wallets, watches, AirPods, protein bars, or anything for your EDC. Strappable through an integrated tether strap, it can attach and lock to just about anything you can think of. I've used it so far on camping trips to go screen-free, as well as a few canoe rides where I still wanted to have my phone around (but avoid it getting wet).

According to recent reports, A significant part of nailing the marks in the outdoor apparel realm is conquering both flexibility and insulation. You know, like this stretchy number from Mountain Hardwear. It’s plenty warm, packs down like a charm, and moves with your natural motions, never pulling or tugging. It helps that it looks sharp and touts elastic cuff bindings to lock in the warmth on those chilly evenings and mornings. This one is a great gift for all types of outdoorsmen, from campers and hikers to anglers and skiers. We found that the climbers here at MH especially liked this one, drawn to the agile design.

In a recent development, this will come in handy for spontaneous adventurers. It’s a handy, pocket-sized kit that has 48 tools useful in almost any outdoor survival situation. Plus, it looks like a freakin' grenade. How gift-worthy is that?

Sources indicate that camp Snap brings a bit of that retro joy to your outdoor adventures. A screen-free device, it makes you wait (in gleeful anticipation) to see the results of your photographic eye. It also comes in cool, earthy color tones and packs well with all of his other adventuring gear. The latest model is 15% thinner, making it even more portable and can knock out 500 images in a single charge. There’s even a kid-friendly setting and don’t worry, you can still access six different filters to get that perfect filter you’re after. With that screen-free business, he really will enjoy his surroundings more and focus less on that instant gratification (while still documenting treks with great pictures).

According to recent reports, no, you’re not saying he’s old with this gift. Rather, you’re rewarding his intrepid spirit and encouraging him to venture even deeper into those topsy-turvy trails. The best way to do so is with a proper pair of trekking poles, which essentially afford an extra set of legs as you navigate harsh terrain. With three sections per pole linked by an internal cord, the design is smart as they fold and the tungsten carbide tips dig into the trail like a pair of eagle talons. Portable, lightweight, and strong, you can pull these puppies out of your pack and deploy them in an instant with a single button press.

In a recent development, the best of the outdoors is usually an off-the-grid sort of thing but a little tech can help you enjoy remote areas even more. Take the latest from Garmin, part of an esteemed line of communication devices that can go deep, deep into the brush. If that outdoorsy someone on your list likes the backcountry, this is a vital addition to his setup. Fit with a digital touchscreen and able to send messages (text and voice) and SOS notes without any service, it’s all about location and safety. The Mini 3 can even send images, use voice commands in various languages, pair up with your smartphone, and send emergency notes 24/7. Oh, and it’s tough as nails, has a strong battery, and can even set you up with the weather forecast.

Here’s a pair for the trail-running novice and seasoned vet alike. The shoe combines comfort, support, durability, and a decidedly stylish look that has no trouble gobbling up mile after mile on the dusty (or muddy, or rocky) trail. On the surface, you get some serious colorways and a toothy but not over-the-top look. Under the hood, an improved midsole that rebounds like an NBA-level power forward and dual mid-foot webbing reinforcements to assist those active feet. And the details add up, from the padded collar to the stay-in-place tongue wings, making for a smooth trek even way, way down (or up) the trail.

It has been revealed that what takes a hoodie into the high-performance echelon and helps it excel there? Extremely breathable and temperature-regulating fleece, genuine ripstop shell fabric, and a pair of warming pockets. Oh, and the raglan sleeves and elastic ends keep things comfortable and secure the warmth. It’s an added bonus that the fit is just about perfect, the hood wears brilliantly, and the whole thing can fend off even the thickest brush and snags. As Marmot rightfully claims, this one breathes like a feather and feels like a fleece. Usually it’s one or the other but not here. Gift this one to that restless outdoorsy soul who stays active year-round.

Taking the enhanced vision category into the unexpected realm of cool, Nocs is up to good work. The latest binocular set fits the bill, with powerful lenses and a textured design that’s easy to carry (and even easier on the eyes). Waterproof, they can accompany any trek, on land or water, in summer or winter, and that goes for all types of outdoors enthusiasts, from casual birders and hikers to backcountry pros and road trippers who like to hit the pullouts and take it all in. Compact with full-size clarity, these binocs do what many twice their size try to do, so store ’em in a small pack or wear ‘em over your neck with ease.

Industry observers note that flannels are a staple in an outdoorsman's wardrobe. If he has yet to try Outerknown's Blanket Shirt, now is the time to gift him one. They come in a ton of colors and are woven in a way that has just the right warmth and softness, without ever going too extreme. Call it the Goldilocks flannel.

Industry observers note that you really can’t miss with a trusty multitool. And there’s no more trusty versions out there than the Skeletool CX from Leatherman. It’s lightweight at just five ounces and sports seven different tools: a steel blade, pliers, wire cutters, a customizable bit driver, and a dual carabiner/bottle opener. That’ll serve anyone’s everyday needs pretty well.

Industry observers note that we love this upcoming book from Max Humphrey, a real celebration of all things Yellowstone. Unlike many coffee table books, this one makes you feel like you’re actually sharing a car with the author and touring the Park, taking in great panoramas of lodges, bison jams, mountain vistas, and more. Perhaps that’s the attention to details and fresh perspective you get from an interior designer like Humphrey. If you like this one, consider his other book on the Great Smoky Mountains.

If they're a runner, they're going to need a few things to continue that before-or-after-work pursuit during the winter months. A headlamp is one of those items, as dark runs need light. The latest offering from BioLite is super light at 2.6 ounces, has a comfortable strap, and holds a ton of charge at 200 hours of runtime. And the best part? I haven't had it shaking or bouncing on me once yet.

According to recent reports, even if he's a man of the woods, AllTrails is a great app to gift him. The Plus membership provides offline maps (more than 450,000 trails around the world), 3D trail previews, and wrong turn alerts. Plus, there's the community aspect of the app where he can log hikes live and earn badges.

When it comes to hard coolers, there are few that do it better than RTIC. The brand's 52-quart wheeled version is a lightweight, uncompromising hauler that can house 78 cans and keep contents cold for up to five days. The all-terrain, puncture-proof tires ensure that his camp meals and drinks know no bounds.

The Best Watches for Men in 2026, Worn and Reviewed by Style Editors

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

THERE IS, PERHAPS, no menswear staple more classic than the wristwatch. Take Koon's gold watch in Pulp Fiction or 007's high-tech timepieces: The best watches for men tell a story and time, while instantly elevating your ensemble. In the watch world, there's a ticker for everyone—whether you're making power moves in the boardroom or chasing the next adventure. Need a leather-strapped dress watch that pairs nicely with your suit? Or maybe you're after a rugged outdoor watch or sports watch to track your laps?

Sources indicate that with many options on the market, finding the right one can feel like diving into a black hole. But don't sweat it—we've tested it all, from everyday essentials to luxury standouts. Whether you're looking to monitor your fitness stats, are after your first watch to wear to the office, need some water-resistance, or have to have dial luminescence in the dark for easy readability, these 7 watches have proven to be the best in style, durability, and function. Step right up, because there's a watch for every guy.

Timex offers the ultimate bang-for-your-buck watch, no question about it. Our testers found it’s the easiest dial to read of all the watch options on this list. That lively blue is sharp enough to catch everyone’s attention but still versatile enough to pair with pretty much any casual or formal fit. It fits comfortably on the wrist and can smoothly adjust if you need to loosen or tighten it. And here’s the kicker: It’s under $100.

Yep, you get all this without putting a dent in your wallet—which can be remarked for nearly all the watches Timex makes. At the push of the crown, the brand's signature Indiglo light-up feature will take over, which means no squinting to see the time for both daytime strolls and late-night outings. The two-tone silver and brass case and mineral glass crystal keep it durable yet lightweight, so it can handle daily wear. Plus, with 10 different colorways, there are options to match your vibe, whether you want something that is "in your face" or semi-low-key.

Read More: The Best Amazon Watches for Men.

In a recent development, seiko delivers a solid mashup of modern and vintage flair in its special edition 5 Sports timepiece. Pulling inspo from the post-war racing boom of the 1960s, the watch dons a checkered flag bezel design, which is not something you see every day. The black dial continues the retro vibes with a white and black checkered circle to frame the indices for the numbers. We also love the red-orange second hand that adds a fun pop of color and harkens back to racing watches and timers of the post-war era.

In a recent development, flip it over, and you’ve got a see-through caseback that lets you peek at the Caliber 4R36 movement—always a cool feature for anyone who loves the horology. We found it has some significant weight to it, but feels balanced and secure on the wrist. It’s an automatic watch, which means no batteries—you just wear it, and it powers itself through your every movement (approximately 41 hours of power reserve). Another bonus: It’s priced at a level that won’t make your wallet cry, which is a steal for the quality you’re getting—something Seiko has become known for.

Attention athletes and adventurers: The G-Shock G-LIDE is loaded with features that keep a record of your progress. First, this bad boy connects to a smartphone app that tracks tides at thousands of beaches, so it’s perfect for surfers, swimmers, or anyone who spends more time in the water than on land. I’ve used it at the pool during the summer, and it crushed it—handled constant splashes without a hiccup, shrugged off chlorine like it was nothing, and the resin strap stayed super comfortable even when wet. Not to mention, timing my laps was a total breeze. All to be expected for the legendary durability of G-Shocks.

Recent findings suggest that in terms of fit, this one islarger, and on smaller wrists, it might look oversized or feel bulky. However, it's an athletic watch, so you'll probably be in workout shirts and not have to worry about fitting it under shirt cuffs.

In a recent development, all things considered, the G-Shock G-LIDE is brimming with other functions that track your laps, cadence, and pace—advantageous for runners, rowers, or gym-goers looking to crush their 2026 (and forthcoming 2027) goals. It’s designed to handle impacts (like any G-Shock), whether you’re wiping out on a wave or accidentally dropping it during a workout. I also found the LED backlight makes it super easy to read in low-light conditions, especially during a late-night jog. Other practical elements include a full auto-calendar, an energy-saving feature to keep the battery going strong, and a design that delivers durability and performance in one.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to field watches, the Hamilton Khaki Field is the gold standard—simple, robust, and packed with style. Speaking of which, the cool blue dial of this version, paired with the brushed steel case, gives it a clean, understated look that’s perfect for everyday wear. At 38mm, it’s compact and classic, sitting just right on your wrist without feeling too bulky.

Recreating the 1960s soldier watch, it’s a timepiece that nails that balance between functionality and style—you could wear it while exploring the outdoors or just heading to a casual dinner. The Super-LumiNova coating on the hands and markers is a game-changer, ensuring the watch is legible in low light or total darkness. We've put it to use during a camping trip and it lit up like a champ when the campfire died down, making it easy to check the time without fumbling for a flashlight. And just last year, Hamilton came out with a quartz version of the KF that's even more affordable and offers the ease of quartz.

It has been revealed that the Bremont Terra Nova is the kind of watch that effortlessly blends rugged practicality with standout style. The cushion-shaped case? It’s got a cool military-meets-modern vibe that makes it stand out without trying too hard. Pair that with the rich green and black striped NATO strap, and you’ve got a watch that screams adventure but still looks sharp enough to wear out on the town.

As for the automatic movement, it features a Glucydur balance wheel (enhances its precision by maintaining consistent oscillations), an Anachron balance spring (offers excellent resistance to magnetic fields), and a Nivaflex mainspring (stores 38 hours of energy to power the watch).

Recent findings suggest that what really makes it a go-to for adventurers and aviators is the oversized Super-LumiNova numerals. These bad boys light up like a beacon, so whether you’re navigating a trail at sunset or checking the time mid-flight in low light, you’ll always have clear visibility. It’s built for people who don’t just sit still—this is a watch designed to keep up with your wildest days and nights while keeping you looking sharp.

In a recent development, the Tudor Black Bay isn’t just any watch—it’s the perfect blend of timeless style, top-notch craftsmanship, and everyday usability. Let’s start with that 41mm steel case. The polished and brushed finish gives it that sophisticated edge while staying tough enough to manage the wear and tear of daily life. Paired with a black rubber strap, it strikes the perfect balance: sporty yet versatile, rugged yet refined. In other words, you could take it to the boardroom, the beach, or the mountains and it’ll look right at home. Not to mention, the strap has a slimmer profile and slightly textured feel that grips your wrist just enough without being sticky or uncomfortable. It's not overly thick or flimsy, and it doesn't soak water or sweat.

Industry observers note that tudor is known for its no-nonsense approach to legibility, and we found the Black Bay is no exception. It’s bold and clean, with luminous markers that practicality glow in low light. So whether you’re checking the time in a dimly lit bar or on an overnight hike, it’s always easy to read. Most mechanical watches offer approximately between 36 and 48 hours, but this one takes it up a level with a 70-hour power reserve. Overall, it’s the kind of watch that will still feel relevant and stylish 20, 30, and even 50 years down the road.

If you’re ready for any action-packed adventure—007 style—the Omega Seamaster Diver 300m is the watch you want. This model is the exact one Bond wears in "No Time to Die," so you know it’s got that "mission-ready" vibe. It’s super lightweight, made from titanium, and has a matching titanium mesh bracelet, so it’s built to last and handle anything—from magnetic fields to pressure underwater. Plus, it even has a Helium escape valve—a small pressure-release system that lets tiny built-up gas particles flee to prevent the crystal from popping off.

During our testing, we noticed the titanium bracelet feels incredibly light on the wrist, which makes a significant difference for all-day comfort. It has a smooth, almost silky texture but isn't as glossy. Another bonus: Titanium is hypoallergenic, so it won't irritate the skin for people with metal sensitivities.

Industry observers note that this watch is a serious upgrade and, yeah, it’s the priciest one on the list, but here’s why it’s worth the investment: It’s a timeless classic with next-level features that will last a lifetime. It’s powered by the Chronometer 8806 movement, so it’s super accurate, and it comes with a 5-year warranty, just in case. In all honesty, it's the kind of watch that'll make you look like a million bucks at an upscale gala or extravagant dinner party. Pair it with a tailored suit and some slick dress shoes for a look that means business.

Sources indicate that the movement is the engine of the watch—it's what keeps it ticking. Below, we've broken down the main three types and their benefits.

Powered by a battery and known for being super accurate, quartz movement is low maintenance, lightweight, and affordable. It's a great option if you just want a reliable watch without the fuss. Quartz watches will only require the replacement of the battery every few years, which is a simple task and costs fairly little.

Sources indicate that backed by the motion of your wrist—no battery required. The gears that make up the movement wind themselves when the watch moves. Automatic watches feel a little more special, sometimes like high-end brands Rolex or Omega, but they'll need to be worn regularly or placed in a watch winder to stay powered. They'll also require consistent maintenance and servicing to keep them optimally running. Automatic watches typically cost more than most quartz watches, but there are many great options that are affordable these days.

Industry observers note that you wind it yourself, usually every couple days. Instead of the movement rotating automatically with motion, the gears need hand-winding to keep the movement running. These watches require attention and typically harken back to the era of vintage, throwback timepieces like pocket watches. Manual watches usually cost more than quartz watches and are on par in price with some automatic watches. They tend to be a little less affordable though.

Think of the case as the body of the watch—it's the shell that houses everything crucial, like the movement (the engine that makes it tick) and the dial (the thing with the numbers and hands). Cases come in different shapes, sizes, and materials. Below, we break down the most common materials used for cases.

Durable, versatile, and scratch-resistant. It's the most common and works for everyday wear.

Lighter than steel but just as strong, making it perfect for sports watches.

Scratch-proof and sleek but can be a bit pricey. It has a modern, luxurious feel.

A strap is any flexible band—made of leather, rubber, nylon, or fabric—that secures the watch to your wrist. Straps can change the entire vibe of the watch. A bracelet, on the other hand, is made of metal—stainless steel, titanium, or sometimes gold—linked together. Bracelets usually feel sturdier and add a bit of weight to the watch, giving a more premium, polished look. The good thing is many watches allow you to swap between a strap and a bracelet, so you can switch up the style depending on the occasion.

Recent findings suggest that classic, comfortable, and stylish. Perfect for dress watches but less durable for heavy-duty activities.

Stainless steel or titanium bracelets are durable and versatile for both casual and formal occasions.

Great for sports and water activities—comfortable and easy to clean.

Sources indicate that when shopping for the best men's watch, features and complications can make all the difference in terms of functionality and style. Ultimately, these details should match your lifestyle. We've broken down some important specs to keep an eye out for, but these are by no means an exhaustive list of everything you could find in some complex watches.

This is the ring around the watch face, and when it rotates, it actually serves a purpose (beyond looking cool). On dive watches, for example, the bezel is used to track elapsed time—turn it to line up with the minute hand before you dive, and you'll know how long you're underwater. Some bezels work for other things, like GMT watches, where they help track a second time zone. But in everyday life, most people just fidget with them because it's oddly satisfying with a ratcheting sound.

In a recent development, water resistance tells you how well your watch can handle moisture. There are two equivalent measurements you will typically find when it comes to this rating. Meters (as in depth) is the first and atmosphere (designated as ATM and measures the pressure of every 10 meters. So the first rating is 30m, which is rated at 3 ATM. This is splash-proof, which means your watch can handle occasional hand-washing or light rain, but don't submerge it. 50m (5 ATM) is good for shallow water activities like light swimming, but no diving. 100m (10 ATM) can handle swimming, snorkeling, and most water sports. 200m+ (20 ATM) is built for diving and serious water activities. Watches like the Omega Seamaster are built specifically for this sort of pressure.

A chronograph is a type of complication added to the watch movement that essentially gives the watch a stopwatch functionality. It's great for timing events, workouts, or even laps around a track. You'll typically see sub dials for seconds, minutes, and sometimes hours. While it adds functionality, it also gives the watch a sporty, complex look. The most famous example of a chronograph is the Rolex Daytona, made famous by watch icon Paul Newman.

Sources indicate that A date window adds convenience—you won't have to check your phone or calendar to know the date. It's a small but handy detail, especially for busy schedules. Watches such as the Seiko 5 or Tudor Black Bay makes this feature feel seamless by blending it into the design.

Luminous markers or hands are a must if you blueprint on wearing the watch in low-light situations, like at night or in darker environments. Watches with Super-LumiNova or tritium tubes glow brightly and for extended periods and make the dial easier to read when overhead light is sparse.

Pay attention to case diameter and thickness. Case diameter is the main number you'll see alongside watches. Generally speaking, around 38-42mm diameter is ideal for most wrists, but larger or smaller watches can suit personal taste. The diameter of cases tends to ebb and flow with watch trends. For the first part of this century, case sizes gravitated over 40mm for lots of watch makers. But in 2026, smaller watches (even down to 32 and 34mm) are en vogue. We like to find a happy medium and suggest trying on different sizes to see what's most comfortable for your wrist.

If you’re rough on your gear or are looking for an everyday wear, opt for a scratch-resistant sapphire crystal (the transparent covering that protects the dial), shock resistance, or robust designs for long-lasting wear.

According to recent reports, our style team, led by Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan, continually tests almost every watch known to man and put them through their paces for everything they’re designed to handle: marathon training, cycling, traveling, hiking, sleep tracking, daily fitness routines, and dressy occasions. To identify the most ubiquitous watches, we relied on our previous experience testing and owning various models, as well as prior expert coverage on Men’s Health.

We considered features such as case material, comfort, battery life, accuracy, dial design and aesthetics, water resistance, and magnetic resistance. Bonus points were given for unique specs that added functionality like a date window or sub dials. Our picks aren't just utilitarian though—they're seriously stylish, making them the perfect accessory for everything from the gym to date nights. In the end, we narrowed it down to 7 standout watches that tick all the right boxes and can provide a timepiece for any type of guy.

15 Best Places to Buy Bedding, Editor Picks (2026)

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that sheets get slept in every night and washed every week (in theory) which means it doesn’t take long to learn which ones hold up under use.
  • Each brand earned its spot for a reason, whether that’s price, a cooling fabric, an unusually wide color range, or embroidery done by hand.
  • For bedding basics that won’t damage the budget, Quince is our first stop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that sheets get slept in every night and washed every week (in theory) which means it doesn’t take long to learn which ones hold up under use. Every retailer here comes recommended by an AD editor or contributor who has lived with the bedding at home for a long stretch: flannel kept on the bed through May, linen hauled to a communal laundromat and back, or a sheet set that survives a dog digging in every night.

Each brand earned its spot for a reason, whether that’s price, a cooling fabric, an unusually wide color range, or embroidery done by hand. Rest assured: they’re all comfy.

For bedding basics that won’t damage the budget, Quince is our first stop. Its European Linen Sheet Set earned our pick for the best affordable linen sheets, and senior shopping editor Nashia Baker has recently added the brand to her list of favorites. “The price point is unbeatable, and I love that they offer bedding sets in beautiful colorways and a variety of fabric options,” she notes. “The quality is also impressive, especially considering the affordability.”.

Made from 100% European flax, the sheets cost a fraction of what competitors charge, thanks in part to Quince’s direct-to-consumer model which skips traditional retail markups. “I love its airy nature along with the gorgeous Bordeaux color that complements the rest of my decor,” notes Baker. The bedding range extends to quilts and coverlets, , and the brand’s down comforter also made our ranking of the best comforters.

Anyone who has paused a Nancy Meyers movie to study the bedroom should start with Serena & Lily. The brand is based in Sausalito, California, but its textured, breezy bedding and decor would look right at home on any coast, Nantucket included. The range covers lightweight linen and crisp cotton percale in pale colors and easygoing prints.

According to recent reports, of all the bedding Baker has tested, the Nantucket Stripe Sheet Set ranks near the top for its light weight and “worn-in texture,” which keeps the linen soft instead of scratchy. The ruffle trim keeps her bed from looking too plain. “The striped mink print does give a seaside vibe, but it’s been neutral enough to layer with any color bed cover without clashing with the rest of my minimal, romantic decor over the few months I’ve tested the set,” she adds. For a top layer, there’s the scalloped Baywood Quilt, which Alpert likes as a light blanket for “when you want to throw something over while you read your favorite Emily Henry book in bed.”.

In a recent development, boll & Branch sheets arrive feeling as if they’ve already been through several wash cycles, without the fraying or pilling that usually comes with that. Contributor Rachel Fletcher tested the brand’s percale, Supima cotton, flannel, and linen, but its signature sateen stood out most for its long-staple cotton and a soft, smooth finish. “That extra-soft feel, paired with the lovely, cooling properties, make them feel like the luxury sheets they are,” she states. Converts can outfit the rest of the room too, with Boll & Branch’s mattresses and bedroom furniture.

Brooklinen started out selling two things, cotton percale and sateen sheets, and has since added cashmere, brushed flannel, and a long list of prints. Pieces come in bundled sets or one at a time, and prices land between the budget brands and the luxury labels. Our editors keep coming back to the linen sheets, which they use in every season.

Recent findings suggest that “Since I don’t live my life on a Greek island, I thought white linen sheets year-round might be a slightly bold move, but the nature of the fiber is versatile and temperature regulating,” indicates AD contributor Madeleine Luckel, who tested the Core Sheet Set. Fletcher sleeps on the Luxe Sheet Set and credits it with keeping her cool. “I’m a hot sleeper with sensitive skin, and they’re really cool on my skin at night, which is a huge relief,” she says. “I love the breathability of these sheets.”.

Recent findings suggest that few bedding brands have tied their name to sustainability as closely as Coyuchi. Its linen sheets are made from certified organic French flax grown without synthetic fertilizers or pesticides, and the brand also offers percale, sateen, and flannel sheets. The earthy color palette is a selling point on its own.

“I love the color, which is what drew me to these sheets in the first place,” says Sam Cochran, global features editor. “They’re the perfect brown—a tad auburn, ever so slightly timeworn in palette.”.

It has been revealed that shopping writer Julia Harrison and contributor Kate McGregor agree: Garnet Hill is their “secret spot” for bedding. Harrison is devoted to the flannel sheets and admits she leaves them on the bed through May because “they’re so soft, I’d rather suffer in my own sweat than switch them out.” The ticking stripe is “perfectly classic—like a true vintage piece, but not actually vintage…that might be tough sell in the bedding department.” Alpert also loves her flannel pick, a duvet cover that “signals a cottagecore moment without going over the top.” Paired with her Ostermoor duvet insert, it’s “like climbing under a layer of meringue.” Garnet Hill specializes in vintage-inspired designs, patchwork quilts especially, made in 100% linen and 100% cotton options at reasonable prices.

Cozy Earth makes breathable bedding for people who run hot at night, and its signature bamboo bedding, made of 100% viscose, are the brand’s best-known example. “I honestly thought these sheets were silk,” indicates contributor Megan Wahn. “That’s how smooth and soft they feel.” Wahn tested them mostly in winter, and despite feeling cool to the touch, they kept her warm. “I’m especially eager to see how they perform in the summer,” she adds. “Something about their smoothness makes me think the summer-night sweats won’t stand a chance.”.

Industry observers note that parachute is where we send anyone after classic, well-made cotton bedding. Its sets and bundles are designed with sustainability in mind, and the percale and brushed cotton are made by artisans at the brand’s factory in Portugal.

“We love [Parachute] because the bedding is designed to provide a hotel-like experience, offering a perfect balance of softness and crispness,” says Stephanie Kraus of Stephanie Kraus Designs, whose clients favor the brand’s linen bedding sets. “They become softer with each wash while maintaining their durability and are super soft to sleep in every night.”.

It has been revealed that fletcher also praises the brand’s commitment to organic, ethically sourced materials; the Organic Cloud Cotton Duvet Set, for one, is made of Oeko-Tex-certified 100% cotton. “I try a lot of bedding in this line of work and the more I do, the more I appreciate ethical and organic production, even if the price tag is a little higher,” she notes.

GreenRow makes charming, long-lasting bedding from recycled and sustainably sourced materials, and it has won over several people on the Shop AD team. Contributor Yelena Moroz Alpert calls the Helena Floral Sheet Set “without a doubt, the softest sheets I own.” She compares the cotton satin to velvet, and the butter-yellow florals and green micro-gingham ruffle make the set prettier still. McGregor, meanwhile, is partial to the reversible patchwork quilt. “It’s the kind of blanket that feels substantial without trapping heat or feeling stuffy,” she notes. “I feel cocooned without a down comforter, but I’m not smothered when I sleep sans AC in the warmer months. It’s a year-round bedding piece for me, especially since the color palette can lean moodier or more cheerful depending on my sheet selection.”.

Industry observers note that rebecca Udall is a newer name and one worth knowing. Her namesake bedding line is built on romantic, careful details, such as soft-colored decorative embroidery along the sheets. McGregor’s current favorite is this scalloped percale sheet set. “The feel is like a washed percale, crisp but forgiving, and I find that the subtle color on the detailed edge gives the perfect amount of visual interest to my all-white bedscape,” she says. If you want less ornament, try the Georgiana duvet cover, with faint ladderstitch detailing hand-embroidered by artisans in Northern Italy.

Hommey, an Australian brand founded in 2020, first caught on with its boldly striped robes and nightwear. It has since carried those designs into cotton and linen sheets and duvet covers. Across both fabrics, there are more than two dozen colors and prints to choose from. For maximalists who want to try color-blocking, the brand’s bolder colorways are a great place to start.

In a recent development, baker tested the brown sugar linen duvet cover and found the stonewashed, Oeko-Tex certified flax smoother and more broken-in straight out of the package than the Quince version she already owned (above). “I won’t get ahead of myself and say it feels like pure silk, but I can confirm that it’s soft and breathable almost like an organic cotton duvet after a few washes,” Baker claims. She pairs the chocolatey shade with burgundy linen sheets for a moodier bed, though it also works as a neutral with lighter sheets in oatmeal, which pick up the cream trim. The one drawback is that the cover has no interior ties, so the insert can shift around inside.

Australian brand Cultiver makes linen sheets and duvets with an easy, beachy look. Its Oeko-Tex certified pieces are an investment, and a worthwhile one. Coverlets are generously sized so they drape loosely, and the envelope-back pillow cases hold their shape without looking stiff. Fletcher has put her set through heavy use and many wash cycles. “Linen is my bedding fabric of choice pretty much 365 days a year, and Cultiver’s high-quality sheet sets do it for me in a way no other brand has. Out of all the sets I’ve tried, this one has stood the test of many washes, my dog digging in them to get cozy at night, and surviving across seasons without feeling worn or threadbare,” she states.

Erica Tanov’s bedding is handmade by artisans in Jaipur, in 100% linen with embroidery drawn from traditional Indian textiles. Harrison calls hers “a lifetime set” that “draws more compliments than anything else in my apartment.” The linen is soft and tough: She hauls this sheet set to her neighborhood laundromat, and it survives the communal machines without damage. It’s the first linen set she’s found to be “city-friendly,” as she calls it. She hasn’t tried the quilts or throw blankets yet, though one already tops her birthday wishlist (this one).

According to recent reports, it depends mostly on how you like your bed to feel and how reliable your thermostat is. If you like the crisp coolness of hotel sheets, try percale. If you like a soft, organic feel, try linen for a breezy texture, or bamboo sheets for something similar to silk. Cotton sheets (like Supima sets) are often the most durable over time, especially after many, many washes. Your warmest options are generally flannel sets, and your coolest are generally bamboo and percale. For a basic setup, we recommend a full sheet set (flat sheet included, people) plus a duvet insert with a cover. The cover protects the insert and keeps it clean, so you’ll generally only need to wash the insert every six months rather than weekly like your sheets. Harrison likes to go one step further with a bed blanket underneath her duvet and above her sheets for a bit of weight and additional warmth. If a fluffy duvet isn’t your thing, a quilt or coverlet can take its place and add a little more weight.

What to Look for When Buying Bedding.

Start with the fiber content on the label. Search for 100% cotton, linen (the more organic, the better), and steer clear of polyesters or more plastic fibers, as they’re likely to pill more promptly and break apart in the washer and dryer.

#167300. Latest Update: How to Do the Walking Lunge for Lower Body Gains

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (953 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Menshealth ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: How to Do the Walking Lunge for Lower Body Gains

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (953 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • YOUR LEGS ARE built for movement, whether you’re running, walking, or jumping.
  • Sources indicate that enter the walking lunge, a truly dynamic lower-body exercise that’s a perfect complement to exercises like heavy squats and Romanian deadlifts.
  • According to recent reports, walking lunges might appear deceptively simple at first, especially if you have done standard reverse lunges before.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

YOUR LEGS ARE built for movement, whether you’re running, walking, or jumping. So why do most go-to leg exercises have you planting your feet in one spot?

Sources indicate that enter the walking lunge, a truly dynamic lower-body exercise that’s a perfect complement to exercises like heavy squats and Romanian deadlifts. (A bonus: It’s a unilateral exercise that isn’t the dreaded Bulgarian split squat.) The walking lunge is one of the few strength moves that truly gets you moving. And in doing so, it exposes muscle imbalances, trains balance and coordination, and challenges your core and upper body more than you might expect—all while attacking every muscle in your legs.

According to recent reports, walking lunges might appear deceptively simple at first, especially if you have done standard reverse lunges before. And in truth, they can be simple. Here, Men’s Health fitness director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S. walks you through the steps to take so that you’re not dragging your feet but making gains toward powerful legs.

Sources indicate that FORM IS EVERYTHING with this move. You’ll want to stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, squeeze your glutes and shoulder blades while keeping your gaze at a neutral spot straight ahead of you.

Industry observers note that once you’re comfortable with this slow and controlled movement, you can add weights to build extra muscle and strength. You can hold them at your sides, hold them by your shoulders in what’s called a front rack position, or grab one heavy dumbbell and hold it to your chest in a goblet position. “Regardless of how you hold the load, make sure to keep your upper-body tight,” claims Samuel. “Grip the dumbbells like you mean it, squeeze your shoulder blades, and tighten your abs, too.”.

Don’t obsess over keeping your torso too upright, though, indicates Samuel. “Especially as you work with heavier loads, don’t be afraid to lean forward slightly,” he says. “That can help you capitalize on your glutes, one of your strongest muscle groups, with each stride.”.

When you’re starting out, says Samuel, aim to take a step that keeps your front shin perpendicular to the ground when you lower your torso into the lunge. But as you grow more experienced, you can play with the length of your stride to chase different goals. “If you take very small steps forward,” says Samuel, “you’ll attack your quads more. Larger steps can help you build hip mobility and knee health. If you take larger steps, go lighter with the load.”.

“The greatest benefits of the walking lunge come from how it challenges us while in motion,” notes Samuel. “In addition to building strength and muscle, every step forward challenges your front leg (primarily tibailis and quad muscles) to decelerate your body in space, and then rapidly work to accelerate into the next step. That’s building coordination and balance, in addition to training almost every lower-body muscle and building serious strength.”.

You’ll work a number of major leg muscles when you do walking lunges, including your calves, hamstrings, quads, and glutes.

SMALL MISTAKES IN your walking lunge technique can turn the lower body exercise into a potential knee-wrecking disaster.

In a recent development, you want to land on the heel of your foot first to provide a strong base for the rest of your lunge position. When you get started with walking lunges, aim for a vertical shin as you lower down to the ground to stay at a 90-degree angle in your front and back legs.

You also don’t want to think of taking a step forward, but stepping out a couple inches by slightly turning your glute. Another adjustment to protect your knee is to shift your knee slightly outward instead of toward the midline. (If you still feel any knee pain during lunges, try a reverse lunge instead).

Recent findings suggest that keep your torso straight and avoid dipping forward, which you may be more inclined to do if you’re carrying heavy weights for this exercise. Your chest should be aligned with the back of your thigh the entire time. As you get up from the lunge, you want to avoid using momentum. That means no shoulder or torso rocking.

THE WALKING LUNGE is a great way to sneak in some movement on leg day if most of your lower-body exercises have both feet anchored to the ground. Load up some weights, and try to aim for 3 sets of 8 to 10 reps per leg, 1 to 2 times a week. You can alternate each leg or finish up all your reps on one leg before switching to the other. Samuel says that will keep more tension and gives you an opportunity to really focus on the muscle.

Sources indicate that an advantage of this move is its versatility, allowing you to do it anytime, anywhere. If you’re crunched for time or in a hotel room, try bodyweight walking lunges. Do it for 45 seconds with a 15 second rest for 5 minutes to break a sweat and build muscle.

Sources indicate that jocelyn Solis-Moreira, MS is the associate health & fitness for Men's Health and has previously written for CNN, Scientific American, Popular Science, and National Geographic before joining the brand. When she's not working, she's doing circus arts or working towards the perfect pull-up.

Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S., is the fitness director of Men's Health and a certified trainer with more than 10 years of training experience. He's logged training time with NFL athletes and track athletes and his current training regimen includes weight training, HIIT conditioning, and yoga. Before joining Men's Health, he served as a sports columnist and tech columnist for the Latest York Daily News.

#167299. Ginger Rogers at Home: 10 Photos of the Golden Age Icon’s Glamorous SoCal Life

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1466 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Architecturaldigest ↗ Open Full Page

Ginger Rogers at Home: 10 Photos of the Golden Age Icon’s Glamorous SoCal Life

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1466 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that while most people race to the hospital to give birth, Ginger Rogers’s mother, Lela, insisted that her baby girl’s first breaths be taken in their Missouri home.
  • Decades after her death in 1995, Rogers is poised to return to the big screen by way of Sabrina Carpenter, who’s set to portray the late actor in the forthcoming, yet-to-be-titled Fred Astaire biopic.
  • According to recent reports, after Rogers separated from her second husband, actor Lew Ayres, in 1936, she and her mother moved in together.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that while most people race to the hospital to give birth, Ginger Rogers’s mother, Lela, insisted that her baby girl’s first breaths be taken in their Missouri home. “The little four-room house at 100 Moore Street was the perfect choice” for the future icon’s July 1911 welcome to the world, Rogers concluded in her 1991 memoir, Ginger: My Story. The star would go on to live with her extended family in Kansas City at 3306 Bellefountain Street; with her stepfather in Fort Worth at 1510 Cooper Street; and once she became a Hollywood sensation, a sprawling Beverly Hills estate. That joy and sense of peace she found in her childhood residence became a defining feature of her California pad. “It was a fun house, a happy house,” Rogers told Architectural Digest in 1994. “I was never angry when I didn’t have to work, because I liked to stay home so much.”.

Decades after her death in 1995, Rogers is poised to return to the big screen by way of Sabrina Carpenter, who’s set to portray the late actor in the forthcoming, yet-to-be-titled Fred Astaire biopic. Tom Holland will star as Astaire. Read on for a glimpse inside the Oscar winner’s off-set life in the places she cherished most.

Rogers on the diving board in 1938.

According to recent reports, after Rogers separated from her second husband, actor Lew Ayres, in 1936, she and her mother moved in together. “I asked Mother if she would like me to build her a house, and if she did, could I live in it with her,” Rogers wrote in her memoir. “The next day she scoured the area for a suitable place to build. She found a wonderful lot high in Beverly Hills on 2.75 acres on Gilcrest Drive in Coldwater Canyon. It had a view that didn’t stop; when the fog burned off late every afternoon, it was possible to see Catalina.” Rogers is pictured at the stunning estate in this 1938 photo.

The actor with her home ice cream fountain.

Recent findings suggest that the Swing Time star added many personal touches to the home, one of which was an elaborate soda fountain. In this 1940 photo, she’s shown whipping up a sweet treat. In her memoir, Rogers recalled all the amenities she installed. “The building took over a year because of labor strikes and material shortages,” she wrote. “When the house was finished, it proved to have been worth waiting for. It had everything I wanted or needed in a house: swimming pool, tennis court, projection room, and my very own soda fountain. Who could ask for anything more?”.

Rogers opened her home tennis court to championship hopefuls so they could get practice matches in.

In a recent development, rogers was an avid tennis player. Though she’s pictured here in 1950 at her Malibu beach house, the actor also had a home court installed at Gilcrest Drive. “On the way to the pool and tennis court were eight sculptured bay leaf trees. Next to the blue-tiled pool was my tennis court. This was my pride and joy,” she wrote in Ginger: My Story. With the knowledge that Rogers had the only en-tout-cas court in the area, the Tennis Association “begged” her to invite young hopefuls for some practice before they went on to championship matches at Forest Hills, Latest York. “I was delighted to open my court to competitors like Pancho Gonzales, Gussie Moran; and, later, Billie Jean King, Jennifer Hood, and Alice Marble slammed a few over the net too,” Rogers stated.

Rogers was known for hosting her Hollywood star friends at home in Beverly Hills.

Recent findings suggest that the Top Hat actor’s Beverly Hills abode was also a hot party spot for Rogers’s A-list friends. “My home was made for entertaining and I gave party after party,” she wrote in her memoir. “Most of them were informal. I’d serve spaghetti and we’d play some night tennis. Alcohol was never served, just cold drinks. One, a mixture of finely crushed ice, 7-Up, and concentrated orange juice, was a real favorite with the tennis crowd.”.

The star had a close relationship with her mother, Lela.

According to recent reports, rogers loved living with her mother, with whom she’s pictured in the circa 1940s portrait on the piano in this 1954 image. The triple threat pushed back against the term “stage mother” in Architectural Digest; she considered her mom to be “my guide and my professor… she was my encyclopedia. She knew what route to take: She helped Lucille Ball along hers too, you know. It would have been hard to have a career without her.” About their Beverly Hills pad, she added, “we both liked the look of a French farmhouse. And I wanted certain specific things: a helpful bath, a tennis court, and my own projection room, where we had eight or ten director’s chairs, so that friends could come over to watch movies.”.

Rogers with a furry friend at home in the 1950s.

The home featured a main house with bedrooms for Rogers and her mom, as well as a guesthouse for visitors. “The house was very bright,” she told Architectural Digest. “I don’t like dark things; even in my clothing, I prefer to be light and colorful—Springtime for Henry has always been my motto,” she explained, referencing the 1934 comedy. In her memoir, Rogers added, “The style was an American farmhouse with Dutch doors opening to cool breezes. The large bay window in the corner of the living room had a view of Beverly Hills and a bit of Los Angeles. Off the living room was a patio for barbecuing on a flagstone area under a beautiful Australian pepper tree. It was a wonderful place to entertain on crisp California nights.”.

Industry observers note that rogers’s home also included a solarium, and bedrooms with scenic views. “On a lower level was an outside entrance to the playroom,” the actor noted in her memoir. “This room had significant windows and comfortable cushions as did the solarium in the hallway to the patio. I read many a book, with apple in hand, buried in those downy cushions.” About her bedrooms, she added, “There were two bedrooms leading from the solarium, one for Lelee [her mother] with a four-posted bed and one for me. My room looked out on the view of Beverly Hills, and I had a beautiful hand-carved mantel for my fireplace.”.

Rogers at work on an oil painting.

Sources indicate that in addition to the stage talents for which she became a star, Rogers was also a painter. Her guesthouse also doubled as a studio. “My studio, which could double as a guesthouse, held all the paraphernalia of my hobbies: painting materials, canvases, paintbrushes, turpentine, pencils, and so on,” she wrote in her memoir. “Whenever there was a lull on set, I’d take out my pencil and sketch,” Rogers added. “I had been drawing for a long time and it seemed to come naturally to me. I found it challenging and relaxing. I never studied drawing or painting, I just did it.”.

In her memoir, Rogers recalled a time when she brought her paintings out for a gallery show. “When I’m not working or traveling, my main source of relaxation comes from my painting,” she wrote. “Gallery owners have wanted to have a one-person show of my work, but I never had the time to organize my paintings. Well, now was the time. Gregg Juarez, a gallery owner and friend of mine, arranged for a show and sale at his gallery in Palm Desert. As we were hanging the paintings for display, I realized these were my children—I couldn’t sell them! Gregg told me I had to sell a few so the customers wouldn’t get mad. I managed to put a few up for sale, but couldn’t part with the rest. So now they are joyously hung in my home for all to see.”.

Rogers was 83 years old when she died in 1995 at home in California.

Recent findings suggest that rogers remained at her home on Gilcrest Drive until 1970, when her mom urged her to sell while she was away working in Europe. “I had been renting it out more than living in it lately, and Mother thought it was financially sound to put it on the market,” the actor wrote in her memoir. “Besides, she remarked it needed a upcoming roof! She handled all the details of the sale…. This was one time I’m not sure Mother knew best. I adored that house on Gilcrest Drive and have regretted selling it ever since.” Rogers died decades later, on April 25, 1995, at her home in Rancho Mirage, per the Los Angeles Times.
